title: test(ui): relax type-level restatements of spec literal unions; keep the two exhaustive pins on their consumers
body:
Fixes #26275

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## What

Type Check UI went red on every ui PR whenever `@objectstack/spec` added a member to a union that a ui test pinned exactly with `Equal<…>`, even when no ui behaviour changed. This PR measures every such pin, decides each one, and relaxes the restatements. The pins over a union that ui is genuinely total over stay exact, and their red now names the ui site that needs the new case.

The surface is test files only: 14 files under `ui/packages/**/__tests__` or `*.test.ts(x)`. No source file, sdui record or published file changes, so it carries `skip-changeset`.

## Population: 85, not 51

The card's figure (51 pins in 31 files at `df8aac41f`) came from a scanner whose list was not published. I re-measured at main `96635f57` with a TypeScript AST scan. It counts every `Equal`-family assertion (`Equal`, `IsEqual`, `Equals`, `TypeEqual`, `Eq`, `Same`, `Exact`, `SameType`, `SameKeys`, `DeclaresExactly`, including file-local aliases) where one argument is a literal union. That gives **85 candidates in 56 files**, including the card's example (`PendingActionStatus` in plugin-chatbot `spec-symbol-batch6.test.ts`). The scan was rerun after #26272 merged and found the same set.

A syntactic scan cannot tell which unions the spec owns, so each verdict comes from an experiment, not from reading. I mutated the built spec declarations (`packages/spec/dist/**/*.d.ts` and `.d.mts`, which ui test configs resolve through `paths: {}`) in three ways:
1. **members:** a new member on every `z.ZodEnum`, literal `ZodUnion` and quoted literal union;
2. **keys:** a new key on every `z.ZodObject` and interface;
3. **tuples:** a new member on every literal tuple.

I then ran `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` on all 10 packages that host a candidate. A pin that stays green under all three probes is one that a spec addition cannot move, so it was not part of the problem.

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Count |
|---|---|
| restatement → relaxed | 12 |
| exhaustive consumer → kept exact, red points at the consumer | 2 |
| kept: a measured drift ledger, not a restatement | 1 |
| kept: probe artifact (the probe desynchronises a tuple from its enum) | 1 |
| kept: green under every probe | 69 |

**Relaxation form.** A relaxed pin becomes `Equal<Exclude<'a' | 'b' | …, U>, never>`, so every member ui reads is still required. Where the old pin also guarded against widening, it is paired with `Equal<string extends U ? true : false, false>` (or the file's existing "is not string" pin), so the union cannot quietly widen to `string`. No assertion about a member ui reads was weakened.

**The two exhaustive pins** stay exact:
- `_ReasonIsTheEnum` (`DroppedFieldsEvent['reason']`, data-objectstack `spec-symbol-batch6.test.ts`). Its consumer is `STRIPPED_LINE` in app-shell `writeWarningToast.ts`, a `Record<DroppedFieldsEvent['reason'], StrippedLine>`.
- `_VisualizationUnionIsTheNineDrawnKinds` (core `normalize-list-view.undrawableBothLegs-9880.test.ts`). Its consumer is `LIST_VIEW_KINDS` in `normalize-list-view.ts`, a total `Record`, plus `ListView`'s `case` list.

Both consumers are typed totally, so they go red on their own, and each pin's comment now names its consumer as the place to add the new case.
